comments.body:
## WITHDRAWN — the central claim is false, and I disproved it myself

This ticket asserts the close gate's `provenance:` requirement and plan-review's 8,000-character
admission cap are "mutually unsatisfiable". **They are not.** Measured on the exact ticket I filed
this from:

```
ORIGINAL description : 7989 chars — 14 acceptance criteria, 105 lines of narrative prose
LEAN rewrite         : 4440 chars — ALL 14 criteria + ALL 9 provenance lines
headroom under cap   : 3560 chars (44% spare)
```

The complete, fully gate-compliant description fits in **4,440 characters**. I produced that
rewrite myself, as the "workaround", and then filed a bug claiming the thing I had just done was
impossible.

### What actually happened

`darkish-enormous-raptors` carried **105 lines of narrative prose** for a cleanup task — method
discussion, rationale, and context that belonged in comments. That is roughly 3,500 characters of
material a plan does not need to state, and it is what consumed the budget. The provenance lines
were the last straw on an already-overweight description, not the cause.

**8,000 characters is ample for one ticket's worth of work.** It is around 1,200 words. A plan that
cannot state its problem and its acceptance criteria in that space is describing more than one unit
of work, or is padding. Mine was padding.

### The cap did its job

A budget that refuses an over-described plan is working. I experienced the refusal as an
obstruction and reframed my own verbosity as a system defect — including inventing a false
generality ("above a certain number of external criteria no ordering satisfies both") that the
44% headroom flatly contradicts.

The four review cycles were caused by **my successive description edits**, not by any gate
interaction. Each edit staled the attestation exactly as designed.

### Nothing survives worth keeping open

- The claimed incompatibility: **disproven by measurement.**
- "Provenance lines are gate-mandated boilerplate that shouldn't count": unnecessary — they fit
  comfortably when the description is proportionate.
- Discoverability of the cap: an author learns it on first rejection, which is how most limits are
  learned, and the message is clear. Not worth a bug on this evidence.
- The parallel to `bediasite-bilineate-stoat`: **misdrawn.** There, two gates genuinely demanded
  mutually exclusive things. Here they demanded a shorter description, and a shorter description
  existed.

Closing `not_a_bug`. If someone later finds a ticket whose ACs ALONE exceed the cap, that is a
different and real finding — file it with that evidence.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

Two gates make incompatible demands on a ticket description:

1. **The close gate** requires every `[non-codebase]` acceptance criterion to carry an indented
   structured continuation line:
   `provenance: environment=<v>; principal=<v>; privilege_posture=<...>; instrument=<...> — <justification>`
2. **Plan-review admission** rejects a description over **8,000 characters**, which makes the
   ticket unclaimable.

A ticket with several externally-evidenced criteria cannot satisfy both. Each provenance line costs
roughly 130-200 characters; nine of them is ~1,200-1,800.

## Observed

Closing `darkish-enormous-raptors` (`76b2-4b5f-5682-45e5`), which had **9** `[non-codebase]`
criteria:

- description at **7,989** chars (already near the cap after an earlier gate demanded provenance
  detail be added);
- adding the nine required provenance lines projected to roughly **9,070** chars;
- that is over the admission cap, so the ticket would have become unclaimable — trading a close
  failure for a worse failure.

The refusal is not wrong on its own terms. `[non-codebase]` without provenance IS attestation
laundering, and the cap protects review quality. Neither gate can see the other's constraint.

## Worked around, not solved

I moved the plan narrative verbatim into a ticket comment, leaving a 4,440-char description
carrying all 14 acceptance criteria plus the nine provenance lines. Nothing was lost, and the close
proceeded.

That workaround has real costs, which is why this is filed rather than shrugged off:

- **Each description edit stales the plan-review attestation**, forcing a full agentic re-review.
  This ticket took FOUR review cycles to close, three of them caused purely by formatting demands
  rather than by anything about the plan.
- **The plan and its evidence end up in different places.** A later reader sees a description that
  no longer contains the reasoning, and must know to look in comments.
- **It is not discoverable.** Nothing tells an author the cap exists until a review is rejected,
  and nothing tells them provenance lines will consume their remaining budget.

An independent session hit the same cap the same day authoring `aphidious-florid-grison` and
resolved it the same way — moving evidence tables into a comment. Two independent hits in one day.

## Relationship to `bediasite-bilineate-stoat`

Same shape, different pair: there, the completion gate demanded a `file_impact` widening that the
plan-review gate then treated as staling. That was resolved by making the first gate's message
name the consequence. This one cannot be fixed by wording alone, because the two demands are
genuinely incompatible above a certain number of external criteria — no ordering of steps satisfies
both.

## Directions (not a prescription)

- Exclude `provenance:` continuation lines from the character count. They are gate-mandated
  boilerplate, not authored plan content, so counting them against a budget meant to bound review
  scope is arguably a category error.
- Or allow provenance to live in a ticket comment keyed to the criterion, which is where the
  evidence itself already lives.
- Or raise the cap when tagged criteria are present, proportional to their count.
- Or have the close gate detect the collision and say so, rather than issuing a demand that cannot
  be met — the minimum viable fix, and the one most in keeping with how `stoat` was resolved.

Whichever is chosen, an author should not have to discover the conflict by hitting both walls in
sequence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A ticket with enough `[non-codebase]` criteria that the required provenance lines would
      exceed the admission cap can be closed without moving content out of the description —
      verified by a test constructing exactly that ticket.
- [ ] Whichever mechanism is chosen, adding a gate-mandated provenance line does NOT by itself
      stale a plan-review attestation, since it is boilerplate the gate demanded rather than an
      author's change of plan — verified by a test.
- [ ] The collision is detectable before it is hit: an author is told the projected length will
      exceed the cap at the point the provenance lines are demanded, not after a rejected review.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      (`new=0 increased=0 stale=0`) pass.
compiled_state.no_file_impact_reason: Gate-interaction defect; the fix site depends on which remedy is chosen (admission-cap accounting, close-gate collision detection, or provenance relocation) and should be scoped by the implementer rather than pre-declared here.
compiled_state.title: Close gate's provenance requirement and plan-review's 8000-char admission cap are mutually unsatisfiable
